column3: Close to the Hebrew; NASB sets the first line in quotation marks as words recalled from God.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB sets the verse in quotation marks as recalled words.
Close to the Hebrew; “has seen” is rendered “sees.”
“I reject” (with no object) is rendered “I retract,” and “on dust” as “in dust.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a reliable thing” is rendered “what is right.”
“I will lift up his face” is rendered “I will accept him,” and “to do folly with you” as “do with you according to your folly.”
Close to the Hebrew; “lifted up the face of Job” is rendered “accepted Job.”
Close to the Hebrew; “turned back the captivity” is rendered “restored the fortunes.”
“His children and his children's children” is rendered “his sons, and his grandsons.”
